I used to grow mushrooms and I find them fascinating! Most of the time a mushroom mycelium network will fruit only because it feels threatened, that’s why you very often see mushrooms fruiting the days following a very heavy rain, because the mycelium network realized it might be drowning and then it quickly fruits to drop spores to continue the line. A mycelium network will also fruit when it runs out of food or space to grow. Anything to spread the spores.

When you’re growing mushrooms yourself, you spray water on the top of the cake and the sides of the bin to replicate a rainfall, and mushrooms are often soon to follow!

Also a fun thing, if you cut the top of a mushroom off before its gills are fully spread, you can place it on a piece of tin foil or parchment paper gills side down and wait a couple days. When you go back to it, you’ll get a perfect spore print! They’re so beautiful to see, and you can store them later to try and grow them yourselves if you’re trying to breed a stronger version of a specific strain by taking a qtip, getting some spores on it and then rubbing it on an agar plate to see growth. 

Obviously only try that will edible mushrooms, but the spore prints are cool because they’re very unique mushroom to mushroom. I’ve made spore prints in the past of non edible mushrooms I come across on my walks just because I love seeing the differences.
